evidence: src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts: `import { toCourse } from '../courses/courses.service';` borrows the course mapper from another service module instead of using a shared mapper or repository abstraction
src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts: constructor injects `@InjectRepository(CourseEntity) private readonly courseRepository: Repository<CourseEntity>` and persists course state directly

src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts enrol(): `const course = toCourse(entity); course.admit(); entity.enrolled = course.enrolled; await courseRepository.save(entity);` hand-writes the reverse mapping, so it is split from toCourse

src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts withdraw(): `new Enrolment(row.courseId, row.studentEmail, row.enrolledAt)` and enrol(): `this.enrolmentRepository.create({ ...enrolment })` map Enrolment inline, unlike the mapper-based Course path

src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts enrol(): `if (!studentEmail.includes('@')) throw new DomainError('invalid', ...)` puts an email rule in the application service instead of the Enrolment domain type
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit is a single file, and its concern (enrolling and withdrawing) holds together. The problem is that it spreads the course aggregate's persistence across two places and works around the abstractions that should own it. EnrolmentsService injects Repository<CourseEntity> directly. It loads the course row, converts it with toCourse (a helper exported from courses.service.ts), calls admit(), and writes entity.enrolled = course.enrolled back by hand before saving. So the entity-to-domain mapping lives in courses.service.ts, while the domain-to-entity write-back lives here. That splits one mapping rule across two modules and skips any course-level service or repository abstraction. Enrolment mapping is also handled inconsistently: Course goes through a mapper function, but Enrolment is rebuilt inline (new Enrolment(row.courseId, row.studentEmail, row.enrolledAt)) and saved as create({ ...enrolment }). Business rules also sit in the service instead of the Enrolment domain type: the email check (studentEmail.includes('@')) and the duplicate-enrolment check. Rules like these are easy to end up duplicated. My confidence is moderate because courses.service.ts and domain/enrolment.ts were not provided.
